mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) over three months signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST shows a sustained increase over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals supply-side weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals stagflation, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when GDPC1 is negative for two consecutive quarters and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in the last month.
